text: Twisted Timbers is a hybrid roller coaster built by American manufacturer Rocky Mountain Construction (RMC) and located at Kings Dominion in Doswell, Virginia. It originally opened in 1994 as a wooden coaster named Hurler, designed and manufactured by International Coasters, Inc., as an exact clone of Hurler at Carowinds. The ride closed for "extensive maintenance" in 2015, and in 2016, Kings Dominion teased that Hurler would reopen in 2018, hinting at a renovation by RMC with the message, "There's really more coming." The park contracted RMC to revamp the aging coaster, during which the wooden track was replaced with steel using RMC's I-Box track technology, enabling more aggressive elements and inversions. The ride reemerged as Twisted Timbers on March 24, 2018, featuring three overbanked turns, three inversions, and twenty airtime moments, and reaches a maximum speed of 54 mph (87 km/h), which is faster than its predecessor. It ranked third among new rides in 2018 in the annual Golden Ticket Awards from Amusement Today. On August 16, 2017, Kings Dominion officially confirmed that Hurler would reopen as Twisted Timbers and open in 2018, with promotional artwork and ride specifications released in a press release. The ride includes a barrel roll drop, similar to Wind Chaser at Kentucky Kingdom. A soft opening was scheduled for March 22, 2018, for media and American Coaster Enthusiasts members, with a second for season ticket holders, but due to inclement weather on March 21, both were held on March 23. The grand opening to the public occurred on March 24, 2018. When Hurler closed in fall 2015, no renovation signs were visible, but on March 25, 2017, RMC I-Box track was spotted in a storage yard, and amateur drone footage four days later revealed track removal had begun. On May 20, new wood and steel supports appeared on the old structure for the first time. On May 21, the park tweeted the first in a series of teasers setting the announcement date for August 16. On August 8, just over a week before the formal announcement and three days before ride details leaked online, the ride's lift hill was topped off. After a winter hiatus, the final track pieces and two custom trains were installed on February 17, 2018, with the signatures of the park's full-time employees placed on the final piece as an "Easter egg." Kings Dominion tested the completed attraction on February 21, and on March 20, four days before the grand opening, the two trains—one blue and one green—tested together. The ride is set in the fictional Hanover Hill Orchard, a rustic apple orchard named after Hanover County, Virginia, where the park is located. Signage throughout the queue tells the story that in 1950, a mysterious force destroyed the orchard and froze it in time, and in the present day, a local businessman has reopened it as it appeared in 1950. Guests are encouraged to tour the abandoned orchard, with the queue line passing mangled trees, flipped farm vehicles, and other signs of destruction. The station is themed as a partially destroyed apple shipping warehouse, and the trains resemble weathered 1937 Ford pickup trucks. Along with the ride's opening in 2018, the surrounding Candy Apple Grove section was rethemed to continue the 1950s orchard theme. Twisted Timbers, previously known as Hurler, is located in the Candy Apple Grove section and takes riders to a height of 111 feet (34 m) before entering a barrel roll inversion and dropping them 109 feet (33 m) down the first hill. It features twenty airtime moments, three overbanked turns, and two additional inversions, including a cutback and zero-g roll. In its debut year, Twisted Timbers placed third in the category of "Best New Ride for 2018" in the Golden Ticket Awards from Amusement Today, and ranked 38th on the publication's list of top 50 steel roller coasters. Amusement Today praised the ride for its dramatic maneuvers, abundance of airtime, inversions, and remarkable smoothness compared to its former life. In June 2018, a woman was hit in the forehead by a mobile phone while riding Twisted Timbers and was taken to the hospital, receiving three stitches.
